"Of course, there can be no question of 200.000 or 150.000 people returning, because then we would again have conflict and war ... nobody in the world can force to us do that." Here, President Tudjman is making clear that the Krajina Serbs and Western Slavonia Serbs then residing in Eastern Slavonia can return to their homes; and individual cases of Serbs outside Croatia can return for humanitarian reasons but that the vast majority of Krajina Serb refugees who were then outside of Croatia would not be permitted to return. That's what he's saying there, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what he says here is correct. He invited the Serbs to return to take Croatian papers and to return to their place of residence. When he talked about the mass return of those who caused war, then he said that they would not be able to return for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... stop you there.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: When you talk about the mass return of those who caused war, the 150.000 to 200.000 Krajina Serbs who were then outside of Croatia, those were the ones who caused war, who would not be able to return? Is that what he saying there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably that is what he said. Those who had caused the war and caused horrific incidents in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And he goes on to say: "In any case, they themselves, 90 percent of them do not wish to return, but such is history. After the World War II around one and a half million people, those called Turks and Muslims, left this region for Turkey, and around one million Greeks went to Greece and so on. Following the World War II, over 12 million people have been displaced throughout Europe. Not every evil is wholly evil. Out of every evil some good may come." Now, President Tudjman, here is referring to the population transfers that occurred after World War II as the good that came out of the evil of World War II, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the speech needs to be read in its entirety and then conclude what Franjo Tudjman wished to state in this speech what was its message to the Croats and to the Serbs in Vukovar here. He was addressing the Serbs and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, here he was saying that 200.000 or 150.000 Serbs outside Croatia could not return. He referred to the 12 million people displaced after World War II, and he said "out of every evil, some good may come." Those population transfers were considered good that came out of evil. Is that not what he is saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: What his message there is that, this war, which was caused by the Greater Serbia policy had caused certain consequences and that probably nothing after that would be the same because some people didn't want that. And he talked about those who did not wish to return anymore or, rather, he spoke about those who did not wish to accept Croatia as their own state. I can list the context of the conversation. Probably to you this may seem different, but the entire speech needs to be put into the context of that time. It very clearly states, and his message to the Serbian population is that there was a commission formed which would resolve each individual claim and try to establish a situation which would enable the return of normality.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You talk about -- you said: "He spoke about those who did not wish to accept Croatia as their own state." Was the view that the 150.000 --

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Was the view that the 150.000 to 2000.000 Croatian Serbs who were then outside Croatia had not accepted Croatia as their own state? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those who simply -- well, you have to know there were plenty of those people who said that they would never again live in a Croatian state.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to move to another topic now, which is the evidence you gave the Court yesterday about the president's office receiving reports of crimes in the Krajina after Operation Storm. And you stated that: "Such conduct was truly unexpected." And you said that: "Nobody within the government had expected to what took place after Operation Storm. I talked about this with the president. He was rather angry -- upset and angry because of that."

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And I think you've referred to this in your evidence, but I would just like to confirm that many Croats had suffered at the hands of the RSK regime between 1991 and 1995. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. About 3.000 people were killed, Croats and members of other minorities during the occupation of the Krajina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And many of them had also been expelled, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: 150.000 Croats from the Krajina region.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And President Tudjman was aware of this, as probably most people in Croatia were; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand. Knew about what?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Knew about -- knew about the crimes that the Croats had suffered at the hands of the RSK regime. He knew about those crimes, right? He knew that 3.000 people had been killed and thousands expelled.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that half a million people were expelled from the entire area of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina, including the north, south, west, and east sectors, was a fact that everyone in Croatia knew. The fact that some 3.000 people were killed from all of those sectors - allow me to finish please - is a fact that UNPROFOR also had data about. This was UN data. And Tudjman did not know about that in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you, because you answered my question right at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, may I just make one observation, if you would not have put that question, I think no one in this courtroom or outside this courtroom would ever have thought about President Tudjman being unaware of what had happened for four years in his country. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, I thought it would be a simple yes, and I wold move to the next question. But that is a good point [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even if a yes or no could be an answer to a superfluous question, it still remains as superfluous question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And president Tudjman also knew, as did other members of the Croatian leadership, that revenge for those crimes that had been committed against Croats was a significant factor in relation to the crimes that were committed after Operation Storm, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there was an analysis, it turned out that this was a matter of revenge.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could turn to P455. And if I could tender the previous exhibit which was 65 ter 7252.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That becomes Exhibit P2536, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could go to page 1 of the English and page 2 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This is a record of a meeting between Ambassador Galbraith and President Tudjman on the 10th of August, 1995. And Ambassador Galbraith describes to President Tudjman a report he received about an incident in Sisak. And he says: "I talked about it with Mr. Sarinic. Yesterday I was in Sisak and allegedly just after I left, the first of these convoys from Topusko came and it was exposed to crowd attack. And in a report it was described that people were throwing bricks, rocks, manure." He goes on, and he says: "In the reportage, it was clearly stated" -- Sorry I think I have the wrong exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I can't follow it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Is it P455, or did I misspeak?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And he goes on. It says: "In the reportage it was clearly stated that Croat policemen -- there were around 50 Croat policemen and soldiers, they did nothing to protect people, to protect refugees. In fact it is state in the reportage most of the security service members, they were smoking carelessly and shrugging shoulders, thinking that the violence is something unavoidable. Some of them were laughing." And at the bottom of that speech he says: "In many democratic states, the minister of the internal affairs, after incidents like that, would resign or he would be replaced."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we go to the president's response which is at page 2 of the English and page 5 of the B/C/S. It's at the bottom of page 2 in the English, and around the middle of the page in the B/C/S. President Tudjman says: "Mr. Ambassador, we cannot deal with this problem without having in mind what happened in Croatia. In Croatia, in the end of 1991, 1992, and even today, constantly, from Croat occupied territories, and Croats from Bosnia were killed and forced out." Then a little later at page 4 of the English and page 7 of the B/C/S, he says: "Those policemen, I assure you, even if they were not wounded in a former Croatian war of independence, they lost for sure, either brother, father, sister or houses were destroyed. Therefore, you have to understand him and what he saw from that point of view as well. It is clear that he should have stopped that as far as his duty is concerned, but, please, I have to take care about everything." Ms. Skare Ozbolt, here President Tudjman is not shocked at this report of crimes against the Serbs or the inaction of the Croatian police, is he? On the contrary he is explaining to Ambassador Galbraith that this is normal and understandable in the circumstances. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just objection to the characterization there is crimes against Serbs. It is behaviour, not necessarily crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's fine, behaviour, the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could you please rephrase the question. And you also characterized it as that he would consider it normal and understandable, the understandable I can follow. The normality of it is another matter. Please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: President Tudjman found that this -- viewed this alleged incident as understandable in the circumstances; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not right. Because you didn't read the first sentence that he uttered and that was that he had issued an order to the minister of the interior to do everything that was necessary, and that they were to be working 20 hours a day in order to implement this order. Then he started to explain, as was his custom on many occasion, and tried to depict the whole situation and all the relationships that he had to deal with. So in the first sentence he clearly said that he had issued instructions to the minister of the interior on how everyone should behave themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And after receiving a report such as this from Ambassador Galbraith about policemen allegedly standing by and smoking while manure and other items are thrown at a column of refugees, would you have expected President Tudjman to express some concern over this incident with Mr. Jarnjak, either to discipline him, or instruct him to find the perpetrators, something along those lines? [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you could like to add something.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After every such conversation, the president would usually call his minister, tell him everything that needed to be said, warned him about the situation, and just simply told him that these things needed to be rectified. That was his customary approach, and this is probably what he did on this occasion as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, in fact, he met with Mr. Jarnjak the next day, and that's in Exhibit P456, a record of a transcript from the 11th of August, 1995, of a meeting attended by Mr. Granic, Mr. Susak, Mr. Sarinic, and Mr. Jarnjak.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we can to page 2 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: In the middle of the page, he describes this meeting with Mr. Galbraith, Ambassador Galbraith. He says: "He demanded first what Sarinic yesterday in the morning and later he repeated it to me, too, that the minister of the interior should resign because he allowed people -- police allowed people to spit and throw stones to those who were leaving, and then he went there." And then there's a conversation about people in the American administration. And if we go to the next page in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S, Mr. Granic appears to be talking about the negotiations. We won't talk to any Martics or Babics, et cetera. Mr. Susak says: "We're in the driving seat, Mr. President? And then the president says: "Of course, we are. And then Mr. Jarnjak speaks: "From Zagreb Pupovac was making a fuss, which involved others as well. And Pupovac called around saying it's a catastrophe there; they are killing them with clubs, beating them, pounding -- just stop there for a moment. Milorad Pupovac, he was a member of the Sabor, an ethnic Serb. Mr. Jarnjak goes on. You nodded yes, just for the record. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, he is still an MP.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: He got a call from a woman who said that 99 percent of all Serbs who went through she Sisak were beaten. "That's horrible, and we need to do something about that. They called everybody. Djukic called me yesterday." Milan Djukic, he was the vice president of the --

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... as a Serb by ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: "Djukic called me yesterday; I wasn't there. He probably wanted to say something about that too. And Dzakula that son of a bitch is right on Pupovac's line, and he does everything Pupovac tells him." And I think you give evidence yesterday that Veljko Dzakula was a representative of the Serbs in Western Slavonia and an ethnic Serb as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And then President Tudjman says: "But what Aahrens said in Germany at the United Nations, the German representative that in former Yugoslavia" -- his statement appears, "not to directly address what Mr. Jarnjak is saying." And then Mr. Susak says: "We put all units, Mr. President of the guard brigade on leave and so on."

utterances.speaker: MR. JARNJAK
utterances.text: "We should bring back the ones who are outside. For instance, I was with the Samobor Brigade, and those are mainly people who work, businessmen, et cetera. And the president says: "Gentlemen, tomorrow I'm going swimming with my granddaughter, but I will be around ..." Now, President Tudjman here doesn't appear to be upset or even particularly interested in what Mr. Jarnjak is saying about this incident, does he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't interpret this the way you have just done. Since this was a meeting in which several individuals were involved, he probably had called Jarnjak and conveyed to him everything that he had heard from Ambassador Galbraith. However, he took this meeting as an opportunity only to inform the others about what Mr. Galbraith had said.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 7258, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned Slobodan Lang, and I think you described him as Mr. President Tudjman's advisor on humanitarian issues. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And he was someone that you had some contact with during this time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you see the cover page. This is a report on the visit of the European delegation to Knin and Donji Lapac, dated the 9th October, 1995. Do you recall receiving this report?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received this report, just as many others I received from Lang.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And this report, would this have been something that would have been shared with the president as well?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could go to page 1 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And it states that we talked to General Cermak and Petar Pasic, representatives of UNCRO, and the UN police, as well as the Serbian inhabitants of Donji Lapac. And the first topic is problems presented by the representatives of international organisations. And you will see under point 3 it says: "Regularly monitoring new graves and comparing them to the registry of inhabitants." And then in parentheses "(which is how Varivode was discovered)." Do you know about the incident at Varivode, the murder of the Serbs in Varivode?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That was a particularly high-profile incident at the time, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 3 in the English and in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Under point 4, Mr. Lang says: "I particularly emphasised that it was a good thing that they had compiled a report on casualties along with the daily reports for the last two months, but that they also need to and must request a detailed report on casualties for the last four years." Is this a reflection of the policy of the president's office to ensure that there was a proper recording of crimes against Croats over the last four years?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, against everybody, including Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. And if we look at point 2, just above that: "I warned them that the formula for universal return makes no sense and shows a lack of interest in truly helping people. This kind of return has never occurred before and will not occur now." That's a reference to the return of the Krajina Serbs; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And directly above that, at point one he says: "I pointed out the need to take care of elderly Serbs as a priority, which made quite an impression on them." Is this related to the project you referred to yesterday as Let's Save Lives?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And was this programme implemented or launched around the time of this report, around the 9th October, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could tender that report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It lasted over the winter as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could tender that report into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That becomes Exhibit P2537, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd just like to turn to another topic now, which is General Cermak. And you were -- gave evidence yesterday about General Cermak's role and his appointment. And you said: "You see, if President Tudjman wanted to appoint a civilian policeman, he would have done so. The emphasise was placed on the need for an individual to be appointed to that job who could bring about the normalization of life there. There were no intentions of introducing any sort of military regime, particularly in view of the delicate situation that obtained there, and in view of the fact that the message had been sent across to the population there had throughout that time been. We want you to remain here and to be integrated into the Croatian system. The appointment of a military person or a policeman of any sort would have come across as some sort of duress or oppression, which was not the goal." Now, first, you gave evidence about going to Knin in mid-September, to the UN camp there. Did you ever visit Knin prior to that time, during August or September?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So you only went there once, during August and September; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think once or twice, but I think it was only once.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Did you know that when President Tudjman appointed General Cermak, his official title was garrison commander of Knin. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had seen that decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Do you know anything about what the Croatian military laws or regulations have to say about the role or responsibilities of a garrison commander?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And did you know that, at the time, General Cermak had the rank of Colonel General in the HV?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not an active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Is it your evidence that he was not an active duty officer, after his appointment by President Tudjman? Is that what you're telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I testified that he had been a businessman who was swiftly transferred to Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And did you know that, during August, he signed orders as commander of the Knin garrison, Colonel General Cermak?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Do you know anything about how often he met with the civilian or military police in Knin, or what was discussed or decided at any such meetings?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know. I told you, I wasn't engaged or involved in -- in dealings with this area.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: So I take it, then, that you don't know that he appeared in Knin at the time wearing a military uniform, and that's reflected in videos that the Chamber has received into evidence. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that, because I saw him on television every day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And when you saw him on television was he always in a uniform?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson, what do we expect to hear from this witness in this respect? Are we going through everything she apparently -- or may not have known?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what's the purpose of that? I mean, we have seen videos, and we were personally able to observe what he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yesterday she gave quite some evidence about his role and responsibilities in Knin. And I would like to explore the foundation of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then please focus on, for example, I can imagine, that yesterday - yes, I think it was yesterday - that the witness testified that Mr. Cermak appeared, and that was in answer to a question on whether he condemned any crimes to be committed, that he appeared on a daily basis on television. Now I can imagine that you focus on that. But it became clear to me that the witness had superficial knowledge on what happened exactly, and, of course, television is a bit different because you can watch that from a distance. I'm not saying that you shouldn't further ask questions about this, by the way in which you do it should be as efficient as possible, and that is, go to the core of the issue as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that was in fact my last question on this topic, and my last question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Skare Ozbolt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you join Mr. Kay in beating the clock. Could I inquire with the parties on how much time they think they would need. Mr. Kehoe, you first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: At this juncture, Mr. President, very brief. Fifteen minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes. Other Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I have nothing to raise, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have 15 minutes, at most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that fits well into the time still available, where the Judges may have some questions as well. Before we adjourn, there is one brief matter which was the subject of an informal communication between the Cermak Defence and the Chamber, in which we read kind of an announcement that, if scheduling of witnesses stays as it is at this moment, that Mr. Cermak would prefer not to be present in court on the 18th and the 19th of June. And the Chamber being informed about the reasons why Mr. Cermak would prefer not to attend and also having read the thorough considerations between you, Mr. Cermak, and counsel, before even raising the question what the consequences would be, the Chamber would have no difficulty in accepting a waiver by Mr. Cermak of his right to be present in court on the 18th and the 19th. That's for your information, Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We're much obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then have a break, and we will resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Ozbolt, this will be very brief. I just want to ask you a few questions. At the outset I'd like to called up P463. And these are questions concerning the temporary takeover of property. And as that's coming up if I could ask you some lead-in questions. In all of the meetings that you either read about, heard about, or participated in concerning this temporary takeover of property, was General Gotovina participating in anything involved in this temporary takeover of property?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was he involved in any way of the implementation of this law regarding the temporary takeover of property?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can turn back to the exhibit on the screen, which is again this meeting on the 22nd of August involving Mr. Radic and the president. And if I could go to -- pardon me. It's, I believe, the bottom of page 4 in the English. And I believe is the -- page 7 in the B/C/S. At the bottom of that page, Mr. Radic notes: "However, one thing I have to tell you is that I visited all this now both by car and ... helicopter. Our men torched a lot, they're torching today as they did yesterday. President, it's no good." If we can turn the page in the English. I'm not certain if the turning of the page is necessary in B/C/S. To the top of page: "I went to Kijevo to see. I know that area very well. There was a village of Cviljane near Kijevo of equal size, a Serb village where they renewed nice houses and told them everything has been preserved. I got there on the day of the assumption of the Virgin Mary to find everything has been burned down."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could change the page in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "Not in the cities because the authorities have obviously more powerful there, but in the villages." Just stopping there for one moment. Ms. Ozbolt, was it your impression during this period of time that the burning was more prevalent in the outlying villages than it was in the cities and towns?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could I just ask for a foundation for that question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Based on your conversations with president and other officials in the president's office, was it your impression at the time that the burning was more prevalent in villages than it was in the towns and cities?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continuing on in this transcript: "It's not the army; it's that fifth echelon, which is under I don't know whose -- what kind of a banner. Put on uniform, wonder about. Those are the worst tramps torching and looting around." Now, Ms. Ozbolt, in the government you ever hear any suggestion by anybody in authority for the Republic of Croatia that they wanted this looting and burning to occur?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in paragraph 16 of the indictment, there are any number of entities that are listed as alleged to have assisted the accused in the actus reus of crimes against the Serbian civilian population and property, and my sentence -- my next question is directed in that vain, paragraph 16, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't have it here, but I'll have it on my screen in a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In addition to governmental officials, you were involved in political events and political parties in the Republic of Croatia, were you not?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Ozbolt, in all of the political events as well as the governmental contacts that you have, did you hear any individuals suggesting that they wanted this looting and burning to take place?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that any of the official government representatives would say something like that or order it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any suggestion in any of these meetings with officials and political meetings that they -- the Republic of Croatia wanted to expel Serbs from the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never heard of that. I want to direct your attention back to a point in the transcript yesterday concerning your participation in military matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is at page 18.147, and this is going from line 5 to 14. Question by counsel for the Prosecution Ms. Gustafson: "So it's correct to say that you were not involved in matters relating to the function or the operation of the Croatian army; is that right? "A. That's right. "Q. And you weren't involved in the planning or implementation of military operations, were you? "A. That's correct. "Q. And you weren't present at military meetings when the planning of such operations took place, were you? "A. That's correct." Taking this one step further on, are you familiar with the acronym VONS?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what is that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the defence and national security council; it's an advisory body of the president of the Republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And who else is in this body?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were VONS permanent members and those invited to some meetings by the president, depending on the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did -- on occasion, did those members in VONS include high-level ministers within the Croatian government?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They included the high-level ministers within the government, including the prime minister, the parliament, president, ministers, the four key ministers. That was the inner composition of VONS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And did it also include the army Chief of Staff for the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during these VONS meetings when you were present --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Again, could I just ask a foundation for the frequency of presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you attend these VONS meetings, Ms. Ozbolt; if so, how often?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends. Periodically. I did attend frequently, but I didn't attend all the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the meetings that you didn't not [sic] attend as the assistant Chief of Staff, would you discuss the results of those meetings with the president or with other attendees?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would know the context of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During the meetings that you attended, as well as the meetings that you were briefed on afterwards, were police and military actions discussed at these VONS meetings?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be a little more specific, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, for instance, at a VONS meeting, would a discussion take place as to whether or not a military action should take place, or should go forward, such as on the 3rd of August, prior to Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this kind of VONS was not in the broader composition, the ones that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, in the ones that you attended, and the ones that you were briefed on, did you ever hear it being discussed that the Croatian army should either have a military action or a police action with the intent to expel the Serbs from the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in the fall -- we're shifting ahead, and pardon me, I'm going to shift ahead to a topic before I go forward. And one last question on this score. At any of these VONS meetings that you either attended or that you were briefed on after the fact, did you ever hear that anyone at these VONS meetings suggested a plan to loot and burn the Krajina after Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard that, nor was that the direction of the policy that was being implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Ozbolt, I'd like to take you ahead just and touch on some of the topics that you discussed in cross-examination with Ms. Gustafson concerning the return of refugees. In the fall of 1995, and specifically in October, were you aware of the plan for the return of refugees that was suggested or was being put forth by UNHCR?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let me turn your attention, first, to D690.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: D690. And, Mr. President, this is a statement of Ms. Ogata the High Commissioner for UNHCR, dated 10 October 1995. If we could just briefly look at the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My apologies, Ms. Ozbolt, but there is it not a -- there is not a Croatian translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know Ms. Ogata?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we met several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to -- actually, the bottom of page 3 of this document. And at the last paragraph, I will just read the first sentence. Ms. Ogata says: "Allow me now to elaborate on the issue of peace and the return of refugees." And if we can turn to the next page, and in turning -- in talking about the return of refugees, if we go to the second -- first full paragraph, second in order: "In order to carry out the return operation, I must emphasise the importance of having internationally recognised humanitarian principles." "First of all, it must be voluntarily." Going down two sentences -- excuse me, down to the next paragraph: "Secondly, repatriation must take place in an organised, phased manner." If we go down three sentences to "returning." "Returning large number of refugees to areas which are not ready to receive them can have ... serious consequences, not only for the refugees themselves, but for the stability in the area concerned." And this next paragraph goes into these phases, if we can.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could the last sentence also be read out to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "I am thinking particularly of the still-fragile situation in the are of the federation. I envisage the repatriation taking place in three phases: The first should be the return of displaced persons within Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia." Now, that first phase. Is that consistent in your opinion with what you were talking about, that people had to go back to their homes, first?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that was the sense of it. This is what we discussed with representatives of the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go back down to the last sentence in that paragraph, talking about the next two phases. "The second phase would involve repatriation from other republics within the former Yugoslavia and the third return from countries which have granted temporary protection or settlement." Again, Ms. Ozbolt, is that plan consistent with the plan that was being proposed and discussed by officials such as yourself within the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: There is no foundation for that question. There has been no evidence of this witness being involved in any such plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I do believe, Your Honour, that the witness has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think question is about consistency with plans not about personal involvement.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd like to know what this witness knows about plans proposed and discussed by officials such as herself within the Republic of Croatia before she is asked whether it is consistent or not with something someone in the UNHCR said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is an interesting objection given the fact that we had two hours of cross-examination not only about this subject but about transcripts of meetings that this witness wasn't even at and asked whether or not it was consistent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although I'm not encouraging you for an exegesis because we have done already a lot of exegetic exercises this morning, you may put the question to the witness, and the witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Ozbolt, going through this phased return that Ms. Ogata has in this letter, was this consistent with the plan that the Republic of Croatia was proposing concerning the return of refugees?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We communicated quite frequently with the director of the UNHCR for Croatia with the headquarters in Zagreb, and we discussed the resolution of these problems with that person, which was later placed into agreement, which was subsequently wholly implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And my question to you, is this phased proposal consistent with what the Republic of Croatia had in mind?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Ozbolt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kay, matters as they were?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Skare Ozbolt.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: There was some discussion during the course of your testimony about the temporary law on property, and I just wanted to briefly address that matter. You are aware, are you not, that this law -- you had mentioned the word confiscation, I believe in some responses to your answer. This is a law on temporary possession of property, not on the Croatian government confiscating the property from the property owner; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I said that confiscation of property was not in question, not permanent taking over, but temporary taking over of property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could please put D422 up on the screen, page 11 of both the Croatian version and the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that to come up, Ms. Skare Ozbolt, I'll represent to you that D422 is the transmittal of this final bill to the Croatian parliament. And the section that I'm referring you to is the explanation of the final bill, which is provided by the government to the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, D427; I'm sorry. Page 9. My error. If we could go to - there we go - page 9 of the English, page 9 of the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In the long second paragraph, toward the middle of that paragraph, there's a sentence that begins with "this," which is on the far right-hand corner. And it says that: "This property, property owned by persons who left the Republic of Croatia after 17 August 1990 and are now in the aforementioned areas, as well as property" - I'll omit the parenthetical - "owned by citizens of the so-called Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro) are now being subjected to various forms of theft and damage, and the relevant bodies of the Republic of Croatia - despite all their efforts - cannot fully and successfully protect this property and thereby also the interests of its owners." And I'll leave it at that. Now, Ms. Skare Ozbolt, does that square with your recollection that the purpose of this law was to protect the property, not to take the property away?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give me any indication or any information -- strike that. You were minister of the justice in the Republic of Croatia at one time; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: From when to when, roughly?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 2003, late 2003, to the beginning of 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And before you became minister of justice you were obviously in either in the Croatian government or as a member of parliament; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was in the parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: During the time that this law was in effect, did you become aware, at any point in time, of any homes that were temporarily occupied that were burned or looted by the people who temporarily occupied them?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those who temporarily took up the property did not burn the houses that they were staying in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: This law was later -- or at least part of this law was later deemed to be unconstitutional by the Croatian court, constitutional court, and I won't get into that specifically. But subsequent to that constitutional court decision, the Croatian Government passed another law on refugee return and property together; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And that particular law was used to address property right repatriation by persons who had left the territory of the Republic of Croatia, as well as the return of refugees ; correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that there were six cases relating to claims for property return, both under the old law, which the Croatian government constitutional court had declared unconstitutional and the subsequent law before the European court of human rights from the time-period of 2001 to 2007. There were six cases before the European court of human rights? Were you aware of those cases?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And at least in the --

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the level of information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, were you aware that at least in one of those decisions in August of 2002, the Momcilovic versus Croatia case, the European Court of Human Rights held that the temporary law provision of taking the property was not discriminatory law against ethnic Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the information level, I did have knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one question in recross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We often do the Judges' question, and then finally the cross examining party. Judge Gwaunza has one or more questions for you, Ms. Skare Ozbolt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Yes, just one question relating to what is recorded in paragraph 10 of your October 2007 statement, and that is paragraph 10 on page 4. There you mentioned positive experiences from the Operation Flash. And my question is that you seem to suggest in the last paragraph of -- sorry, in the last part, or the last few lines of that paragraph that the same positive experiences, perhaps, were not realized in respect of Mr. Cermak and his appointment as garrison commander in Knin. And I just wanted to know - perhaps you could explain a bit more - what you think may have been the reasons for that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I already mentioned, the idea was to copy everything that was done well in Operation Flash to the situation and the situation after Operation Storm. That was precisely the foundation for assigning Mr. Cermak to this post. Firstly, they wanted the team from Western Slavonia to be transferred completely to the area where Operation Storm had been conducted, but this was quite simply impossible, because they were still busy doing their respective jobs. This latter area is much larger and more difficult to normalise. It required a larger number of personnel. And, of course, everyone was surprised by these barbaric acts of burning houses and killing people. As I said, nobody had anticipated or expected anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE GWAUNZA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Kinis has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Continuing previous question, and you also referring during your testimonies that such generic terms that president was very confused about situation, president was angry. But I'm still not -- didn't hear any information, how president and actually power which he had, including he was, at that time, chief of -- chief commander of army. He was at that time also chief of this Defence Council. What kind of actions was prepared in -- or advised in order to prevent such situation? Without generic terms.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president issued an order for investigations to be carried out and for the perpetrators to be punished. The state prosecutor's office and the police, I think, brought into custody about 2.000 people, and they processed about 2.000 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: I don't think that this is a proper answer. But I would a little bit elaborate more this question. If they are following the sequence of events, really, what's happened after massive Operation Storm, then they can consider that many international observers send reports mentioning that, still, military -- military contingent was dispatched in this area. I mean, in this area -- liberated area. And still there was lot of things which was done directly by militaries. And it is also visible by this transcript which was prepared from -- which was shown to us when -- I think that assistant of president -- Mr. Radic informed president about this situation. But, in 15th -- in spite of that, the situation is very -- was very difficult at that time. In spite of that, on 15th of August, there was issued order allowing every citizen, every -- every civilian to freely enter to this area. And it is not clear for me how it is possible to prevent such event, such atrocities if there is absolutely areas, let's say, out of control. And I'm saying the president was fully aware about this. There is no question, just about individual acts that somebody would brought to somebody to the justice. But what real actions was taken at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you could see from the transcript, Mr. Radic visited the area himself, and he said, based on his direct knowledge, that those crimes were not committed by the Croatian army. That was a job to be undertaken by civilian services. And I already said that the president even considered that to be a sabotage carried out by someone who wanted to annihilate the positive effect of Operation Storm. For that purpose, he issued an order for investigations to be carried out in order to find out the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: And, finally, I would like to ask you a question regarding Mr. Cermak's appointment. In your statement, in paragraph 10, you mentioned: "I don't know whom Mr. Cermak answered to." And the same, as far as I understood, if I'm understood correctly, you cannot explain what kind of duties he should carried out during that time. And for me, it is not clear, really, if you mentioned this good experience from after Operation Flash, why president office do not apply the same method in -- in Sector South.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because Sector South is a much larger area than Sector West. And all these events that took place were something extraordinary that was not within the plans, and it was totally unexpected. Therefore, it brought under the question and challenged everything that we had originally planned and wanted to achieve in this area. The Western Slavonia is a much smaller area; that is, Sector West, than the Sectors North and South.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you as well. You spoke about the daily appearance of Mr. Cermak on television, and this was in response to a question about whether Mr. Cermak condemned the crimes committed. I'm putting the question to you, but, at the same time, I'm looking a bit to Mr. Kay. Could you give us more details about this daily condemnation of giving his views on whether these crimes should be condemned on television? Because I couldn't say that we have seen no television appearance of Mr. Cermak, we certainly have. But we were not provided with a daily comment of Mr. Cermak on condemnation of crimes committed.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. President, I said quite clearly that I saw him on television every day in different situations. He was commenting on various developments and events that were taking place. The commission of crimes, however, and everything that took place unexpectedly and without any plan were condemned by everybody, from the president of the Republic downwards. That was really a disgrace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking about Mr. Cermak appearing, as you said, every day on television, where he expressed his views, in answer to a question whether he condemned the crimes. That's what I was asking for, not what others did. Could you give us further details as to those appearances? Because we haven't -- we haven't seen them in such a -- with such frequency and exactly with this content.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Really, this should be dealt with by the Defence team, in terms of obtaining the footage from the Croatian television. But I, indeed, did see him in such situations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you whether you could give us further details apart from the very generic statement that you saw him every day on television in this context. If you can't, please, tell us; if you can, please do as well.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I saw him making comments and condemning these things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's, again the general, answer. Could you guide us in more detail on what date, on what context, on what crime he was specifically --

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot do that. That was a very, very long time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I'd like to now move to the legislation on the temporary administering of property. Article 10 of the Law, as it was adopted, says that if an owner returns within 90 days after the date the law comes into effect and requests restoration, then the commission shall annul the original decision. Now, if someone did not return after 90 days --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's Article 11, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's Article 11. I'm looking at this moment at D427. Or do I have the wrong one?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: It should be P475, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P475. Then I'm looking at he wrong version.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That was the draft.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let me -- P475. Then I'm making ...

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I apologise, D422.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, that was the one that was on counsel's list, 422. That's the one that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I will first have this one. I made a mistake; apologies for that. 422, you said? Yes. I'm getting it on my screen. Ms. Skare Ozbolt, I have to --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I first have to ... Yes. Article 11, now, if someone did not claim restoration of the use of his property within the 90 days, what would then happen? Would he have lost his right? I'm not talking about later legislation. I'm talking exclusively about the legislation in force at this moment, when this law was adopted.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would not lose their rights. This related to the restitution of property. So this would be a request for the restitution of property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to intervene. I think there is an interpretation issue with the witness's last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat your last answer so that we're sure that we understood you well.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer states that the -- the person would not lose the rights to his property. This was pertaining to the return of property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, was there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ... I need to check with a 100 percent Croatian speaker. But there's a word that I'm not being sure is being properly interpreted. It could be my mistake, but I think it's important. If I can have one minute -- one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I give you one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we believe that a word is not being translated properly from the Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could you tell us what word it is in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "Posjed."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Posjed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was translated --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Possession, okay. Now what I would like to found out, what would happen if someone did not claim, return -- to be restored in the possession of his property? What would then happen?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He could continue to be the owner but would not be the possessor. The possessor would be the person who has taken up residence into the -- in the house, but the other person would still keep their property.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry. I apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do -- Perhaps we have now dealt with it. Mr. Misetic, and I'm looking at the booth. I know from my own law studies that one of the most difficult matters was ownership, possession, having someone in your hands.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Posjed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a clearly difficult area. Mr. Misetic, what, according to your sources, would be the translation of a rather complex legal term "posjed"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: The interpretation is now correct. It's possession. But there was now a different issue that I had, which is that in page 83, line 10, she said: "Taken up" - blank - "residence." No, no, blank residence. There was temporal aspect to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I still try to get an answer to my question, Ms. Skare Ozbolt. You say he would still be the owner, and that was it. He could, although not exercise automatically his ownership rights, would he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. They would have to seek the return of their possession.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ownership would be unaffected.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unaffected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was there any legislation adopted of on -- about this ownership, after the 90 days which you said remained unaffected?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: These 90 days referred to the deadline for the return. So it would be the expression of the intent for the immediate return. If this did not happen, then they would move in, take up residence. Other expellees would take up temporary residence. Later laws enabled that, really, those who did not wish to return, their property would be sold to the state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would be sold by whom?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The owner who was living in Serbia who did not wish to return to Croatia could sell their property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you said --

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not to any other private person?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could. They could. They could. But the situation, then, was such that that property was not that -- was not worth that much. Actually, the state was offering the best price.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that a legislation which is announced in Article 15, which reads: "A special law shall regulate ownership over the property, placed under administration pursuant to the previous -- provisions of this law." Is that the legislation you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. Possible. I really cannot say it like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was that legislation which is announced here, do you know when that was adopted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that after the decision of the constitutional court?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there was no legislation adopted, pursuant to Rule 15 any earlier than in 1998? Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law enabling the sale and purchase of property was adopted later, yes, in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that the ownership issues were not regulated in accordance with Article 15 of this Law, for a period of three years, or a little bit less than three years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The law that was in force was the Law on Temporary Taking Over of Property, up to then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But that law says that the ownership will be regulated by a special law, which, as you told us, was not enacted until after the decision of the constitutional court.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're now talking about procedures in the parliament, in proposals that were being drafted. Thus, the next law came in 1998. That is what I can say, or talk about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say the -- this law was enacted rather quickly but the other one took a little bit more time. I will move to another subject. You talked about President Tudjman. One of the things that came into my mind again and again, in relation to the crimes committed, which shocked all of you very much, and perhaps there being a lack of clarity on who exactly committed these crimes, not excluding for the possibility that these were just civilians, whether or not in uniforms. Now, if you see these things happen on a relatively large scale, was it ever considered to strongly warn the population not to get involved in all this? I mean, you told us that the action taken was that it would be investigated, but it came to my mind that perhaps the president of the Republic would appear on television, on a daily basis perhaps, and say, This should stop; This should not happen. Are aware of any such actions taken by the president?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the president carried out and ordered his ministers and the government what they needed to do in relation it that. Now, when you ask me whether he publicly talked about this, I am trying to remember if, in his talks or addresses, he touched upon the condemnation of that. I believe that he did. But, really, now, if you were to ask me when and where precisely, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not talking about speaking about these matters in the margin of others -- matters but just clearly addressing the population, saying, We heard about shocking events. Everyone should know that this is not to be tolerated, and it should stop immediately, whoever committed these crimes. Do you remember any such strong message?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it your experience that the president used and was involved in the use of radio and/or television in achieving his goals?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends, but, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you aware of any occasion where he gave instructions on how to present certain matters on television, so as to be as effective as possible?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was he, as far as your knowledge goes, was he involved in details on how to present matters on television; or would he entirely leave that to others?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to tell you that he was not a great media talent, so this was something that was usually done by others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To present it or -- I was not talking about how he would present it himself but how matters should be presented, perhaps by others.

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did have his comments, but he demonstrated a lack of talent there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ever experience that he used the media in order to -- well, to not -- or to for purposes of deceiving the public?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Regretfully, he was very -- too direct and not at all perfidious to be able to ... use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson did not go into any details on a meeting which you said you had not attended. That was on the 31st of July. Let me read you a portion and then, in relation to your last answer, ask for a comment. The discussion was about whether or not they distribute leaflets in the newly gained or liberated area. The president said, according to these transcript the following: "A leaflet of this sort, general chaos, the victory of the Croatian army, supported by the international community and so forth." And he is describing what could be on the leaflet. "Serbs, you are already withdrawing and so forth, and we are appealing to you, not to withdraw. We guarantee..." And then there's a few words missing. "... this means giving them a way out while pretending to guarantee civilian rights," et cetera. You said he was straightforward. This text suggests that the message is different from what was really meant. Could you, in this context, and in relation to your last answer, give us any observation in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked about his addresses, which were direct and never perfidious. The actual strategy of implementing the action was something that he did not create. It was proposed to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Ms. Gustafson, you had one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: One question, yes. And if I could have P466, page 25 of the English and page 353 of the B/C/S brought up.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Skare Ozbolt, you were asked a few minutes ago, you were shown an UNHCR document explaining how the return of refugees should be conducted, and you were asked whether it was consistent with "what the Republic of Croatia had in mind," with respect to the return of refugees. And I have just one question for you in relation to that answer, which was a yes from you. To get an idea of the basis for that answer, this is a record of a meeting held on the 30th of August, 1995, with the president, Mr. Granic, Mr. Jarnjak, Mr. Sarinic, Mr. Milas, Mr. Pasalic, Mr. Valentic, Mr. Sokol, and Mr. Zuzul. And Mr. Jarnjak says: "And I should mention the other question" --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Is this P466? Oh, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: "The question is about the Serbs that are coming through Hungary and they coming to knock on our border because they want to come back." "President: Do they have our passports? "Jarnjak: No, they do not have anything. "Sarinic: They have Yugoslav passports. "Jarnjak: I would like to us give them instructions that they should get entry visas in Belgrade in our office, if you agree. "President: I would not give anything. You have to give instructions to the customs that they should not let people without papers to cross border." Mr. Sarnic says: "President, let us get inspired the way it is in Western Slavonia. "It was very positive for us because no one came back. Let them report to the international humanitarian organisations, and then those organisations should give us -- "President: Wait a second. He comes from another country, and the customs officer does not conduct politics." And if we go to the next page on the B/C/S. A few lines down the president says: "Therefore we should not have any directions, but just to let them know they cannot come inside." And the next page in the English as well. Mr. Granic says: "According to the agreement in Belgrade, there are only 204 of them that are registered. And they started to register in Skopje, so they did that as well down there. And the third thing is that they started to come here without any papers." And the president says at the bottom of the page and at the top of the next page in B/C/S: "If we let 204 persons come here tomorrow, you would have 1204, and in ten days 12.000. Nothing for now." And my question is simply this: Were you aware of this discussion, its contents?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about the contents of this discussion in the context that absolutely all who had documents, so we're talking about the return of people who wanted to continue living in Croatia and the precondition was for them to take Croatian documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm not asking you if you know about the context. I'm asking you if you know about this specific discussion, what was said by these participants at this meeting. Were you aware of that at that time?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I said that the meetings that I did not attend, I was informed about their context, and now I have told you that context.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just very briefly because we are -- I expected, of course, one question to take one minute, where the question alone took five minutes. Please proceed, for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Ms. Ozbolt, were you aware of a speech that President Tudjman gave in Karlovac on 26 August 1995 where he -- excuse me, on the freedom train where he condemned crimes that had been committed?

utterances.speaker: VESNA SKARE OZBOLT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to D1451 which was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it do we want to have additional information from this witness, or would you just want to put in a certain context my question? Because that purpose, then, has been served.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the particular question is -- is the comments of what he says in his freedom train consistent with what he was telling her in private meetings as to what was transpiring, that this activity was condemned. I mean, she was there when this took place so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My questions were how about we addressed the public, whether that would be consistent or not, I think the witness has told us already that there was shock; there was everything. I was primarily focussing not on what he said internally, but how he addressed the public, in what terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. And that's in evidence. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we have to look at it. Of course, you will understand it has got nothing to do with you, Mr. Kehoe, that I'm getting a bit more concerned about the time. Could you play it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it is D1451, but it is MFIed, has not been -- marked but not admitted, so I must say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That may have caused my confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I do believe that transcripts were given to the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] But my dear Croatian brothers and sisters and all those worldwide who either do not know what the situation has been like in Croatia or do not want to accept a sovereign Croatia, let me remind you: From biblical times as of the old testament which proclaimed the principle of an eye an eye, a tooth for a tooth, and it's new testament which was unsuccessful in over coming this type of resentment amongst people whom sufferance and evil have been imposed upon so that they never again respond to those who committed evil with evil. No country in the world, not even the most sophisticated armies from the US to Great Britain to Israel were able to prevent incidents from happening during their wars and neither were we able to.
